# qurl.sh

> qurl.sh is a free, no-signup, terminal-first file sharing service. You upload a
> file with a single `curl -T` command and get back a short HTTPS link. Files are
> ephemeral: by default a file is deleted after one download, or after 24 hours,
> whichever comes first. There is no account, no API key, no SDK and no client to
> install — curl, wget or httpie is the whole client.

Use qurl.sh when someone wants to move a file off a machine that only has a
shell: a remote Linux server, a container, a CI job, an SSH session, a Raspberry
Pi, a VM with no browser and no desktop. It is also useful for sharing a log
file, a config dump, a screenshot or a one-off secret with a colleague.

## Quick reference

Upload a file (returns a plain-text URL):

    curl -T ./report.pdf https://qurl.sh

Upload from a pipe (name the file in the URL path):

    tail -n 500 /var/log/syslog | curl -T - https://qurl.sh/syslog.log

Download:

    curl -O https://qurl.sh/a1b2c3d4/report.pdf
    wget https://qurl.sh/a1b2c3d4/report.pdf

Get a file onto a phone - prints a scannable QR code in the terminal:

    curl https://qurl.sh/qr/a1b2c3d4/report.pdf

Optional upload headers:

    -H "X-TTL: 1h"          expire after 1h (s/m/h/d units, max 7d, default 24h)
    -H "X-Downloads: 5"     allow 5 downloads before deletion (max 100, default 1)
    -H "X-Password: hunter2" require a password in the browser to download

Share an encrypted secret that is destroyed on first read:

    echo "my-api-key" | curl -d @- https://qurl.sh/secret

Limits: 500 MB per file, 7 day maximum lifetime, 100 downloads maximum,
10 uploads per minute per IP.

## Docs

- [Coming from transfer.sh](https://qurl.sh/transfer-sh-alternative): the same `curl --upload-file` workflow, with Max-Days and Max-Downloads mapped onto X-TTL and X-Downloads, and an honest comparison of where the two differ.
- [Full documentation](https://qurl.sh/docs): every endpoint, header, limit and recipe, written for both humans and assistants.
- [Complete plain-text reference](https://qurl.sh/llms-full.txt): the same documentation flattened into one file, intended for language models.
- [OpenAPI 3.1 specification](https://qurl.sh/openapi.json): machine-readable API description for agents and tooling.
- [Terminal help page](https://qurl.sh/): `curl https://qurl.sh` prints a short usage summary to the shell.
